findings.body: Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-arg call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments 5 for 3..4); emoji resizing fails and the job errors out. The `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` method added just above is dead code.
findings.failure_mode: Method redefinition silently shadows the older signature, producing a runtime ArgumentError on existing call sites.
findings.impact: Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-arg call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments 5 for 3..4); emoji resizing fails and the job errors out. The `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` method added just above is dead code.
findings.root_cause: A second self.downsize with a different arity was added without removing/updating the original 4-argument definition and its callers.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a single downsize method (e.g. `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) and update app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb to pass "100x100", instead of defining two methods with the same name.
findings.title: Duplicate self.downsize definition overrides 4-arg version and breaks ResizeEmoji job
findings.trigger: Any call to the existing 4-argument API, e.g. Jobs::ResizeEmoji#execute calling OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts) when an emoji is uploaded.

raw_findings.body: Attachments larger than the configured max_attachment_size_kb pass client validation and are fully uploaded before the server rejects them, while any file above 10MB is blocked even when the site setting allows it; the alert also reports a wrong "10240 kB" limit. It also breaks the existing test test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6 "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded", which sets max_image_size_kb = 5 and asserts max_size_kb: 5.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Client validation diverges from server validation and from site settings, and an existing JS test assertion no longer holds.
raw_findings.impact: Attachments larger than the configured max_attachment_size_kb pass client validation and are fully uploaded before the server rejects them, while any file above 10MB is blocked even when the site setting allows it; the alert also reports a wrong "10240 kB" limit. It also breaks the existing test test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6 "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded", which sets max_image_size_kb = 5 and asserts max_size_kb: 5.
raw_findings.root_cause: The configurable per-type limit lookup was replaced with a hardcoded constant that applies to attachments as well as images.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep reading the per-type setting (Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']) for attachments, and only relax the limit for images that the server can downsize (e.g. Math.max(setting, imageDownsizeLimit) applied to type === 'image').
raw_findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcodes 10MB and ignores site settings
raw_findings.trigger: A site configured with max_attachment_size_kb (default 3072) where a user selects a 5MB .zip/.txt attachment, or a site with limits above 10MB uploading a 12MB image.

raw_findings.body: The user is told the maximum size is 10240 kB even though the server/proxy limit is smaller, so retries with a 8MB file keep failing with the same confusing message.
raw_findings.failure_mode: User-visible error message states a size limit that does not match the enforced limit.
raw_findings.impact: The user is told the maximum size is 10240 kB even though the server/proxy limit is smaller, so retries with a 8MB file keep failing with the same confusing message.
raw_findings.root_cause: The site-setting based limit used in the error message was replaced by an unrelated hardcoded constant.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore use of Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb (or the effective proxy limit) when formatting the file_too_large message for the 413 case.
raw_findings.title: 413 error handler reports hardcoded 10MB instead of configured image limit
raw_findings.trigger: Web server (nginx client_max_body_size) returns HTTP 413 for an upload on a site whose max_image_size_kb is 3072.

raw_findings.body: FileHelper.download stops writing after ~10MB, so the stored upload is a truncated/corrupt file (or a needlessly rejected upload) regardless of the administrator-configured limits.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent truncation of downloaded API uploads on sites whose configured limits exceed 10MB.
raw_findings.impact: FileHelper.download stops writing after ~10MB, so the stored upload is a truncated/corrupt file (or a needlessly rejected upload) regardless of the administrator-configured limits.
raw_findings.root_cause: A configurable limit was replaced with a magic constant that no longer tracks the site settings used elsewhere for the same purpose.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the cap from settings, e.g. [SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb].max.kilobytes (optionally multiplied by an explicit downsize allowance constant), instead of a literal 10.megabytes.
raw_findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring configured size settings
raw_findings.trigger: An API client posts url= pointing at a 15MB image or a 20MB attachment on a site configured with max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb above 10MB.

raw_findings.body: `convert -resize 80%` rewrites the .svg tempfile as raster/MSVG output, so the subsequent Upload.create_for SVG branch (Nokogiri parse of the file) finds no valid <svg> node and the upload fails with "size_not_found" or stores a corrupted SVG.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid SVG upload is destructively rewritten and then rejected or stored corrupted.
raw_findings.impact: `convert -resize 80%` rewrites the .svg tempfile as raster/MSVG output, so the subsequent Upload.create_for SVG branch (Nokogiri parse of the file) finds no valid <svg> node and the upload fails with "size_not_found" or stores a corrupted SVG.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new condition uses the generic is_image? helper without excluding vector SVG files that other code paths deliberately never pass through ImageMagick resizing.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Skip the downsize loop for SVG, e.g. add `&& filename !~ /\.svg$/i` to the condition, mirroring the SVG special-casing in Upload.create_for and OptimizedImage.create_for.
raw_findings.title: New auto-downsize loop also runs ImageMagick on SVG uploads
raw_findings.trigger: A user uploads an .svg file larger than max_image_size_kb (FileHelper.is_image? returns true for "svg").

raw_findings.body: gifsicle rejects the percentage geometry, convert_with returns false, the file never shrinks, the loop burns 5 gifsicle invocations, and the upload is finally rejected by the size validator.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Downsizing silently no-ops for animated GIFs and the upload fails after wasted work.
raw_findings.impact: gifsicle rejects the percentage geometry, convert_with returns false, the file never shrinks, the loop burns 5 gifsicle invocations, and the upload is finally rejected by the size validator.
raw_findings.root_cause: A percentage geometry string was introduced for a call that can dispatch to gifsicle, which only accepts WxH for --resize-fit.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: For the animated path compute explicit pixel dimensions (or use gifsicle's `--scale 0.8`); e.g. pass "#{(w*0.8).to_i}x#{(h*0.8).to_i}" instead of a percentage.
raw_findings.title: Percentage geometry "80%" is invalid for the animated gifsicle downsize path
raw_findings.trigger: allow_animated_thumbnails enabled and an oversized .gif upload whose tempfile path ends in .gif (e.g. the API url= path, where FileHelper.download preserves the extension), so optimize() selects downsize_instructions_animated → `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`.

raw_findings.body: Each such upload spawns five external ImageMagick/gifsicle processes that cannot reduce the file, adding seconds of CPU per request and giving an attacker a cheap amplification vector before the upload is rejected anyway.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Repeated futile subprocess execution per failing upload.
raw_findings.impact: Each such upload spawns five external ImageMagick/gifsicle processes that cannot reduce the file, adding seconds of CPU per request and giving an attacker a cheap amplification vector before the upload is rejected anyway.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new retry loop only checks file size and attempt count, discarding the boolean success result of downsize.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Capture the return value and break out of the loop when downsize returns false, e.g. `break unless OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`.
raw_findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure return value and retries up to 5 times
raw_findings.trigger: Any oversized image where OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (missing/failing convert, unsupported format, gifsicle error).

raw_findings.body: Regressions such as the changed OptimizedImage.downsize arity, the SVG path, or the loop's exit conditions ship undetected; nothing asserts that an oversized image is accepted and shrunk.
raw_findings.evidence: # allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size
raw_findings.failure_mode: Review/CI cannot detect breakage of the newly introduced upload downsizing behavior.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions such as the changed OptimizedImage.downsize arity, the SVG path, or the loop's exit conditions ship undetected; nothing asserts that an oversized image is accepted and shrunk.
raw_findings.root_cause: New downsizing behavior and the changed OptimizedImage.downsize signature were added without accompanying specs.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a controller spec that stubs SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to a small value, uploads the logo.png fixture, and expects OptimizedImage.downsize to be invoked (and the upload to succeed), plus a spec for OptimizedImage.downsize's new dimensions argument.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for the new automatic image downsizing path
raw_findings.trigger: spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb has no example uploading an image larger than max_image_size_kb, and a repository-wide search for "downsize" under spec returns no matches.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R55 changes `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes` for API URL downloads. Sites with limits >10MB will have downloads truncated. Different location and purpose than JS client validation.

validated_findings.body: `convert -resize 80%` rewrites the .svg tempfile as raster/MSVG output, so the subsequent Upload.create_for SVG branch (Nokogiri parse of the file) finds no valid <svg> node and the upload fails with "size_not_found" or stores a corrupted SVG.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Valid SVG upload is destructively rewritten and then rejected or stored corrupted.
validated_findings.impact: `convert -resize 80%` rewrites the .svg tempfile as raster/MSVG output, so the subsequent Upload.create_for SVG branch (Nokogiri parse of the file) finds no valid <svg> node and the upload fails with "size_not_found" or stores a corrupted SVG.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new condition uses the generic is_image? helper without excluding vector SVG files that other code paths deliberately never pass through ImageMagick resizing.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Skip the downsize loop for SVG, e.g. add `&& filename !~ /\.svg$/i` to the condition, mirroring the SVG special-casing in Upload.create_for and OptimizedImage.create_for.
validated_findings.title: New auto-downsize loop also runs ImageMagick on SVG uploads
validated_findings.trigger: A user uploads an .svg file larger than max_image_size_kb (FileHelper.is_image? returns true for "svg").
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R64 uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` which returns true for SVG per lib/file_helper.rb:31. The downsize loop at R67 runs ImageMagick on SVG, potentially corrupting it. Upload.create_for has explicit SVG handling that would be bypassed.

validated_findings.body: gifsicle rejects the percentage geometry, convert_with returns false, the file never shrinks, the loop burns 5 gifsicle invocations, and the upload is finally rejected by the size validator.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Downsizing silently no-ops for animated GIFs and the upload fails after wasted work.
validated_findings.impact: gifsicle rejects the percentage geometry, convert_with returns false, the file never shrinks, the loop burns 5 gifsicle invocations, and the upload is finally rejected by the size validator.
validated_findings.root_cause: A percentage geometry string was introduced for a call that can dispatch to gifsicle, which only accepts WxH for --resize-fit.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: For the animated path compute explicit pixel dimensions (or use gifsicle's `--scale 0.8`); e.g. pass "#{(w*0.8).to_i}x#{(h*0.8).to_i}" instead of a percentage.
validated_findings.title: Percentage geometry "80%" is invalid for the animated gifsicle downsize path
validated_findings.trigger: allow_animated_thumbnails enabled and an oversized .gif upload whose tempfile path ends in .gif (e.g. the API url= path, where FileHelper.download preserves the extension), so optimize() selects downsize_instructions_animated → `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R67 passes "80%" to downsize. For animated GIFs, downsize_instructions_animated calls resize_instructions_animated which uses gifsicle with `--resize-fit #{dimensions}`. gifsicle doesn't accept percentage geometry, causing failure.

validated_findings.body: Each such upload spawns five external ImageMagick/gifsicle processes that cannot reduce the file, adding seconds of CPU per request and giving an attacker a cheap amplification vector before the upload is rejected anyway.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Repeated futile subprocess execution per failing upload.
validated_findings.impact: Each such upload spawns five external ImageMagick/gifsicle processes that cannot reduce the file, adding seconds of CPU per request and giving an attacker a cheap amplification vector before the upload is rejected anyway.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new retry loop only checks file size and attempt count, discarding the boolean success result of downsize.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Capture the return value and break out of the loop when downsize returns false, e.g. `break unless OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`.
validated_findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure return value and retries up to 5 times
validated_findings.trigger: Any oversized image where OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (missing/failing convert, unsupported format, gifsicle error).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R66-68 shows loop ignores downsize return value. When downsize fails (returns false per convert_with), loop continues all 5 iterations wastefully before upload rejection.

validated_findings.body: Regressions such as the changed OptimizedImage.downsize arity, the SVG path, or the loop's exit conditions ship undetected; nothing asserts that an oversized image is accepted and shrunk.
validated_findings.evidence: # allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size
validated_findings.failure_mode: Review/CI cannot detect breakage of the newly introduced upload downsizing behavior.
validated_findings.impact: Regressions such as the changed OptimizedImage.downsize arity, the SVG path, or the loop's exit conditions ship undetected; nothing asserts that an oversized image is accepted and shrunk.
validated_findings.root_cause: New downsizing behavior and the changed OptimizedImage.downsize signature were added without accompanying specs.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a controller spec that stubs SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to a small value, uploads the logo.png fixture, and expects OptimizedImage.downsize to be invoked (and the upload to succeed), plus a spec for OptimizedImage.downsize's new dimensions argument.
validated_findings.title: No test coverage for the new automatic image downsizing path
validated_findings.trigger: spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb has no example uploading an image larger than max_image_size_kb, and a repository-wide search for "downsize" under spec returns no matches.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap is a stylistic/process observation, not a concrete defect introduced by the patch. Absence of tests doesn't constitute a bug in the code itself.
